title: Grateful Dead Live at Stanley Theatre on 1972-09-28

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear Bill‑board recording of a blazing 9/28/72 show with a monster “Other One” and stellar jams throughout.
ai_review.review: The tape captures one of the peak ’72 performances – a tight first set highlighted by China Cat→Rider, Playin’ and an inspired Greatest Story Ever Told, and a second‑set that erupts into a legendary He's Gone → The Other One → Me & Bobby McGee sequence.  The soundboard source is remarkably crisp, with only the Loser segment showing the usual SBD hiss; overall the audio quality lets the band’s high energy and superb interplay shine.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews rate the show 5 stars, praising its energy, setlist flow and standout jams; recording comments are uniformly positive about clarity with only minor SBD glitches, yielding a high combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, vibrant mix from Bill's board; occasional SBD hiss on Loser and early songs, but overall clear instruments and good separation.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Tight first set with strong transitions (China Cat→Rider, Playin'), followed by a second‑set that builds into a soaring jam suite (He's Gone → The Other One → Me & Bobby McGee) and closes with classic closers; overall pacing is praised as “tight” and “high‑energy”.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring guitar tone, wah‑wah wizardry on The Other One and GDTRFB, occasional vocal mix low but his solos described as spellbinding.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly called “smokin’”, delivering powerful bass bombs during The Other One; many reviewers note his fire as a hallmark of the show’s greatness.
band_member_comments.Bob: His rhythm guitar is noted as high in the mix with superb counterpoint and tone, especially on Brokedown Palace and throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming described as excellent, providing perfect propulsion for jams like The Other One.
